# Error codes

Every response with a 4xx or 5xx status has the same body, the error envelope
(PRD FR-API-04):

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_failed",
    "message": "The request is invalid.",
    "details": {
      "errors": [{"location": "body.colour", "message": "unexpected property"}]
    },
    "request_id": "0199e2c4-5b7a-7d43-9f0e-3c1d2a8b6e51"
  }
}
```

- `code` is one of the codes below. A code keeps its meaning and its
  status once it is released, so clients branch on it.
- `message` says what went wrong, for people. It may change, and is
  not for programs to read. It is in the language that the request's
  `Accept-Language` header asks for, if the server has a catalog for it,
  or else in the instance's default language, `STORYCREEP_DEFAULT_LOCALE`
  (PRD FR-I18N-02), and the response's `Content-Language` header names
  the language. The messages below are the English ones.
- `details` is an object whose keys the code decides, or is absent. It
  is for programs, so the messages in it, as in `details.errors`, are
  in English.
- `request_id` is the request's ID, which is also in the
  `X-Request-ID` response header and in every line the server logs
  about the request.

## Codes

| Code | Status | Message | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_request` | 400 | The request is malformed. | The request body is not valid JSON, or not one JSON value; it has a key twice in one object, text that is not UTF-8, or values nested more than 256 deep; or a required body is missing. `details.errors` lists each problem with its `location`, such as `body`. |
| `invalid_id` | 400 | An identifier is invalid. | An identifier does not decode, or is the identifier of another type of entity, such as a board's identifier where a node's is expected. `details.reason` says why: `missing_prefix`, `unknown_prefix`, `wrong_prefix`, `character`, `length`, or `overflow`, as in `schema/ids/README.md`. |
| `invalid_cursor` | 400 | The pagination cursor is invalid. | The `cursor` query parameter is not a cursor that the same list returned as `next_cursor`. |
| `unauthenticated` | 401 | Authentication is required. | The request has no credentials, or credentials that are wrong. A route that needs a signed-in user answers with it to a request without the session cookie that `POST /api/v1/auth/login` sets, or with the cookie of a session that has ended: signed out, revoked, unused for `STORYCREEP_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, past `STORYCREEP_SESSION_LIFETIME`, or of an account that can no longer sign in. The answer then clears the cookie. A route that takes an API token answers with it, and a `WWW-Authenticate` header of the `Bearer` scheme with `error="invalid_token"` (RFC 6750), to a request whose `Authorization: Bearer` token is not one, or is revoked or expired, or whose owner's account is not active or is no longer a member of the token's workspace (PRD FR-AUTH-04 AC4); a session-only route answers so too, as it would answer `session_required` to a valid token. A route that takes an API token also sends the `Bearer` scheme's challenge, without an `error`, to a request without credentials or with the cookie of a session that has ended. A `Bearer` credential that does not start with `scp_` is not taken for a token, and the request is authenticated by its session cookie instead. `/metrics` answers with it to a request without `STORYCREEP_METRICS_TOKEN` as its bearer token, and its `WWW-Authenticate` header names the scheme. |
| `invalid_credentials` | 401 | The email address or the password is wrong. | `POST /api/v1/auth/login` was given an email address that belongs to no account, a password that is not the account's, or the address of an account that cannot sign in, such as a suspended one. The answer is the same for each, so that it does not tell whether an address has an account (PRD FR-AUTH-01). |
| `csrf_failed` | 403 | The request lacks the session's CSRF token, or came from another origin. | The request changes something, with a method other than `GET`, `HEAD`, or `OPTIONS` (PRD FR-AUTH-02 AC5). Either it was made to a route that needs a signed-in user with the session cookie but without the session's CSRF token, which `POST /api/v1/auth/login` and `GET /api/v1/auth/session` return as `csrf_token`, in its `X-CSRF-Token` header, or a browser sent it, to any route, signing in included, from another site or from another origin of the same site, as its `Sec-Fetch-Site` header says, whatever its credentials. Browsers send that header only to `https` URLs and to loopback addresses, such as `localhost`, so with a plain-HTTP `STORYCREEP_PUBLIC_URL` of another host only the CSRF token is checked, on the routes that need a signed-in user. |
| `wrong_password` | 403 | The current password is wrong. | `POST /api/v1/auth/password` was given a current password that is not the account's, so the password stays as it was. |
| `insufficient_role` | 403 | Your role does not allow this. | The signed-in user's role does not allow the operation (PRD §5.6). An operation of a workspace is allowed by the user's role in the workspace, as only an `owner` or an `admin` changes its settings, invites, removes members, or changes their roles, and creates, deletes, or restores its projects; an operation of a project by their role on the project, their grant on it or else their role in its workspace (§5.5), as only an `owner` or an `admin` of the project changes its name, description, or settings, or archives it. A project grant never authorises an operation of the workspace, as a `viewer`'s `admin` grant on a project lets them neither delete it nor manage its grants (FR-TEN-04 AC4). A user who has no role in the workspace or on the project that the route names, as one who is not a member of the workspace, or a `guest` without a grant on the project, is answered with `not_found` instead, so that the answer does not tell that it exists (§5.5). |
| `insufficient_scope` | 403 | This API token does not hold the scope that this needs. | The request was made with an API token that does not hold the scope that the route needs, nor a scope that implies it (PRD FR-AUTH-04 AC2): `snapshot:read` to list the token's workspace and its projects and to read a project, which every scope but `export:read` implies, `project:read` to read a project's assets, which `project:write` implies, and `project:write` to change a project's settings and to upload an asset. `details.scope` names the scope that the route needs, and so does the `WWW-Authenticate` header, with the `Bearer` scheme's `error="insufficient_scope"` and `scope` (RFC 6750 §3.1). A token never does more than its owner's role allows either, which is answered with `insufficient_role` when the token holds the scope. |
| `session_required` | 403 | This needs you to sign in. An API token cannot do it. | The route takes no API token, whatever its scopes, and needs the session cookie of a signed-in user instead, which `POST /api/v1/auth/login` sets (PRD FR-AUTH-04): every route of an account, its session, sessions, password, and email address, of a workspace's members, invitations, project grants, settings, and usage, of creating a workspace, of creating, deleting, and restoring projects and the trash, of API tokens, and of the instance admin, so that a token cannot make another, change a credential, change who has access, or administer a workspace. Every other route that needs a signed-in user takes a token that holds its scope, as its description says. |
| `owner_required` | 403 | Only an owner of this workspace may do this. | Only an `owner` of the workspace may do this, and the signed-in user is an `admin`: grant the role `owner`, by a role change or an invitation, send an invitation as `owner` anew, demote or remove an owner, or set or remove an owner's grant on a project, which would replace their role there (PRD §5.6, FR-TEN-03 AC4, FR-TEN-04). |
| `owner_not_grantable` | 400 | A project grant cannot make someone an owner. Choose admin, editor, commenter, or viewer. | A project grant was asked for with the role `owner`, which is a role of the workspace alone (PRD FR-TEN-04 AC5): a grant is `admin`, `editor`, `commenter`, or `viewer`. Nothing changes. `details.errors` names the field, with its `location` and a `message`, as for `validation_failed`. |
| `signup_closed` | 403 | Registration is closed on this server. | The instance's signup policy is `closed`, so `POST /api/v1/auth/register` creates no account, whatever the request holds (PRD FR-AUTH-01 AC3), and nor does `POST /api/v1/invites/register`, with an invitation or without: only an account that exists already accepts an invitation then (FR-TEN-02). The policy is the one that `STORYCREEP_SIGNUP` sets, or else the one that first-run setup chose, or else `closed`. |
| `invite_required` | 403 | Registration on this server needs an invitation. | The instance's signup policy is `invite`, so only an invitation creates an account, and `POST /api/v1/auth/register` creates none, whatever the request holds. `POST /api/v1/invites/register` registers an account with an invitation's link. |
| `setup_required` | 403 | This server's first-run setup has not been completed yet. | The instance's first-run setup has not completed, so `POST /api/v1/auth/register` creates no account, and nor does `POST /api/v1/invites/register`, whatever the signup policy and whatever the request holds, so that the first account is always the owner that setup creates (PRD FR-ADMIN-02 AC4). An upload of an asset is refused too, unless `STORYCREEP_ASSET_STORAGE` names where the files are stored, as setup may yet choose a bucket for them (FR-ASSET-01), which an account that `storycreep create-user` made before setup would otherwise have stored files outside of. `POST /api/v1/setup` completes it. |
| `invalid_setup_code` | 403 | The setup code is wrong. The server writes it to its log while setup is pending. | `POST /api/v1/setup` was given a setup code that is not the instance's, so setup stays pending. The server writes the code to its log while setup is pending (PRD FR-ADMIN-02). |
| `instance_admin_required` | 403 | Only an instance admin may do this. | The route belongs to the instance-admin area, which only a signed-in instance admin may use (PRD FR-ADMIN-03 AC1), and the signed-in user is not one. A workspace's `owner` or `admin` is not an instance admin. |
| `email_not_configured` | 403 | This server does not send email. Ask an instance admin for the link instead. | The instance sends no email, because neither `STORYCREEP_SMTP_URL` nor first-run setup gave it an SMTP server, so it cannot email the link that the request asks for (PRD FR-AUTH-03). The answer is the same for every email address. An instance admin gives out the links as text instead, which `POST /api/v1/admin/password-reset-links` and `POST /api/v1/admin/verification-links` issue, and `GET /api/v1/instance` says whether the instance sends email. |
| `email_configured` | 403 | This server emails its links to each account's own address, so it gives none as text. | The instance sends email, so it emails its links to the account's address, and an instance admin takes none as text (PRD FR-AUTH-03). `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset` and `POST /api/v1/auth/email-verification` email them. |
| `email_unverified` | 403 | Verify your email address first, with the link that was emailed to you. | The signed-in user has not verified their email address, which the instance requires before they create a workspace, where it always sends email (the `EmailRequired` capability, as in hosted mode; PRD FR-AUTH-03). The link that `POST /api/v1/auth/email-verification` emails verifies it. |
| `token_invalid` | 400 | This link is not valid. Ask for a new one. | The link's token does not exist: it was mistyped, or it was deleted, as a change of the password deletes the account's reset links that have not been used (PRD FR-AUTH-03 AC4), or as an expired one is deleted after a while, or it was replaced, as sending an invitation anew replaces its link. Or it is the token of another kind of link, or its account can no longer use it, as one that is suspended, or one whose address is no longer the one that it verifies, or its invitation's workspace no longer exists. |
| `token_used` | 400 | This link has been used already. Ask for a new one. | The link has been used already, and a link is used once (PRD FR-AUTH-03 AC2). |
| `token_expired` | 400 | This link has expired. Ask for a new one. | The link has expired: a link that verifies an email address lasts 24 hours, and one that resets a password an hour (PRD FR-AUTH-03). |
| `invite_email_mismatch` | 403 | This invitation is for another email address. Use the account of that address. | The invitation is to another email address than the account's, or than the one that the registration names, and only an account with that address may accept it (PRD FR-TEN-02 AC3). A link invitation, which is to no address, may be accepted by whoever holds its link. |
| `not_found` | 404 | The resource does not exist. | No route matches the path, or the resource it names does not exist, or is in its workspace's trash, as a deleted project is to every route but the one that restores it (PRD FR-PROJ-01 AC3), or the signed-in user's role in it, or in its workspace, is none, as it is for a user who is not a member of the workspace, or the request's API token does not cover it, as a token of another workspace, or one narrowed to another project, does not, so that the answer does not tell that it exists (PRD §5.5, FR-TEN-04 AC6, FR-AUTH-04 AC3). |
| `slug_taken` | 409 | This slug is taken already. | Another workspace has the slug, which is unique on the instance (PRD FR-TEN-01 AC3), or another board of the project has it, in the project's trash or not, which a board's is unique within (FR-PROJ-02 AC1). `details.errors` names the field, with its `location` and a `message`, as for `validation_failed`. |
| `folder_not_empty` | 409 | This folder still holds folders, boards, variables, or components. Move them out of it, or delete them, first. | A `folder.delete` command names a folder that still holds folders, boards, variables, or components that are not deleted, so nothing of its batch is applied (PRD FR-PROJ-02). Move them out of it, or delete them, first; what is in the trash does not count, a variable of a board in the trash among it. `details.errors` names the field, with its `location` and a `message`, as for `validation_failed`. |
| `key_taken` | 409 | Something else has this key already. | Another entity of the scope that a key is unique within has the key, of those that are not in the project's trash: another variable of the variable's scope, among the project's global variables for a global, or among its board's for a board's (PRD FR-VAR-01), another component type of the project, another attribute definition of the definition's type (FR-COMP-01 AC3), or another component of the project (FR-COMP-02 AC1). A command creates the entity with the key, or changes its key to it, moves a variable to a scope where another has its key, or restores an entity from the trash, or a component's type with it, once another has taken its key. A deleted entity's key is free. `details.errors` names the field, with its `location` and a `message`, as for `validation_failed`. |
| `component_type_in_use` | 409 | Components of this type are not all in the trash. Delete them first. | A `component_type.delete` command names a type of which a component that is not in the project's trash is, so nothing of its batch is applied (PRD FR-COMP-01). Delete the type's components first; a type goes to the trash only once each of its components is there, and restoring one of them restores it. `details.errors` names the field, with its `location` and a `message`, as for `validation_failed`. |
| `board_referenced` | 409 | Jumpers on other boards lead to this board. Confirm to delete it all the same, and leave them broken. | A `board.delete` command names a board that jumpers on the project's other boards, which are not in its trash, target the nodes of, and does not confirm the deletion, which would leave them dangling, so nothing of its batch is applied (PRD FR-PROJ-02 AC2). `details.jumpers` lists the first 100 of them, in the order of their IDs, each with its `id`, its `board_id`, and its `title`, and `details.jumper_count` says how many there are, which `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/boards/{board_id}/referenced-by` lists in full. Warn of them, and send the command again with `confirm` to delete the board all the same: the jumpers then keep their targets, which the validation reports. `details.errors` names the field, with its `location` and a `message`, as for `validation_failed`. |
| `last_owner` | 409 | A workspace keeps an owner, so its last owner cannot be removed or demoted. Make another member an owner first. | The change would leave the workspace without an owner whose account is active, and a workspace keeps one (PRD FR-TEN-02 AC2): its last owner cannot be removed or demoted. An owner whose account's deletion is pending does not count (FR-GDPR-02). Make another member an owner first. |
| `already_member` | 409 | This account is a member of the workspace already. | The account is a member of the workspace already: the one that an invitation's email address belongs to, or the signed-in user, who accepts an invitation of a workspace that they belong to, which then stays open. |
| `invite_exists` | 409 | This email address has an open invitation to the workspace already. Send that one again instead. | The email address has an open invitation of the workspace already, one that has been neither accepted nor revoked, whether or not it has expired. Send that one anew, or revoke it first. |
| `limit_exceeded` | 409 | This would take the workspace past one of its limits. | The change would take the workspace past one of its limits, so it is not made (PRD FR-ENT-03): a limit of its plan, or a cap that the instance puts on every workspace (`STORYCREEP_WORKSPACE_LIMITS`). `details.key` names the limit, as the plan file does, such as `members`, `projects`, or `storage_bytes`; `details.usage` is how much of it the workspace uses, and `details.limit` the most that it may use (FR-ENT-03 AC1). The storage limit, `storage_bytes`, which an upload passes, is answered with `storage_limit_exceeded` instead. `details.upgrade_url` is the public site's page that offers the plans, `/pricing`, where the instance both bills for plans and serves the public site, as hosted mode does unless `STORYCREEP_PUBLIC_SITE` is `off`, the limit is the plan's rather than a cap of the instance, and another plan allows more. A self-hosted instance never sends it (FR-ENT-03 AC2). A workspace past a limit already, as after its plan changed, keeps what it has, but cannot add more. |
| `revision_conflict` | 409 | This has changed since you last saw it, so nothing was changed. | Commands of the batch expect revisions of entities that the entities no longer have, because they changed after the client read them, so nothing of the batch is applied (PRD FR-API-03 AC3, ADR-006). Every `expected_rev` of a batch is checked against the entities as they are before the batch, not as an earlier command of it would leave them, so an entity that the batch creates has no revision to expect. `details.conflicts` lists each command's entities whose revisions are not the ones that its `expected_rev` names: the command's index in the batch as `command`, its `command_id`, and its `type`, and the entity's `id`, its `expected_rev`, and `exists`, which is `true`, with the entity's `current_rev`, or `false`, without it, for an entity that no longer exists, as one that was purged from the trash or never created (FR-OFF-04 AC5). `details.states` holds the state of each of those entities that still exists, the entity as it is now, by its `id`, once, however many commands expect a revision of it. An entity in the trash exists, and its state says that it is deleted. To make the change anyway, make it again on the current state, as a new command with an ID of its own and the current revisions. |
| `project_archived` | 409 | This project is archived, so it cannot be changed. Unarchive it first. | The project is archived, and an archived project is read-only, so nothing of the change is made (PRD FR-PROJ-01 AC2). Unarchiving it, deleting it, and restoring it from the trash are the changes that it takes. An owner or admin of the project unarchives it with `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/unarchive`. |
| `invite_expired` | 410 | This invitation has expired. Ask the workspace's admin to send it again. | The invitation has expired: it lasts 14 days from when it was made, sent anew, or emailed (PRD FR-TEN-02 AC1). An owner or admin of the workspace sends it anew. |
| `invite_revoked` | 410 | This invitation has been revoked. | An owner or admin of the workspace revoked the invitation, or removed the member who made it, who was last given its link as text, as by sending it anew, or whom it invites, which revokes it, and it no longer works (PRD FR-TEN-02 AC1). |
| `invite_accepted` | 410 | This invitation has been accepted already. | The invitation has been accepted already, and an invitation is accepted once. Reading it with its link, or registering with it, answers so, and so does accepting it, but for the account that accepted it, which `POST /api/v1/invites/accept` answers with its membership again while it is still a member. An owner or admin of the workspace can neither revoke it nor send it anew. |
| `method_not_allowed` | 405 | The method is not allowed for this resource. | A route matches the path, but not the method. The `Allow` header lists the methods it takes. |
| `request_timeout` | 408 | The request body did not arrive in time. | The client did not send the whole request body within the route's time limit. |
| `request_too_large` | 413 | The request body is too large. | The request body is larger than the route accepts, 5 MB unless the route says otherwise (PRD NFR-SEC-07), or, for an upload of an SVG image, the file that the server would store once it has removed what it does not allow is larger than the upload's limit (FR-ASSET-02). `details.max_bytes` is the limit. |
| `storage_limit_exceeded` | 413 | This file would take the workspace past its storage limit. | The upload would take the workspace past its storage limit, `storage_bytes`, so it stores nothing (PRD FR-ASSET-02 AC4, FR-ENT-03): its plan's, or the cap that the instance puts on every workspace (`STORYCREEP_WORKSPACE_LIMITS`). A file that the workspace stores already, in this project or another, takes up no more, and is never refused so. Uploads that run at once are each checked against the usage before any of them adds to it, so together they may take the workspace past its limit by as much as their own files (FR-ENT-02). `details` are those of `limit_exceeded`: `details.key` is `storage_bytes`, `details.usage` how many bytes the workspace's files take up, `details.limit` the most that they may, and `details.upgrade_url` the page that offers the plans, where `limit_exceeded` would have it. |
| `unsupported_media_type` | 415 | The request body is not in a supported format. | The `Content-Type` of the request body is neither `application/json` nor a type ending in `+json`, such as `application/merge-patch+json`, and the route takes JSON, as every route but an upload of an asset does, whose body is the file, whatever its `Content-Type` says. A body sent without a `Content-Type` is read as JSON. |
| `validation_failed` | 422 | The request is invalid. | A parameter or the body does not match the route's schema: a field that the schema does not have, which is never ignored (PRD FR-API-01 AC2), a missing field, a value of the wrong type, or one out of range; or a field's value is not one that the route takes, such as a registration's email address that is not one, or, for a batch of commands, one that the project's state does not take, or one that would take the batch's undo, which a client sends back as a batch to undo it, past what a request can hold (`POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/commands`). `details.errors` lists each problem with its `location`, such as `body.name` or `query.limit`, and a `message`. |
| `idempotency_mismatch` | 422 | Some of these changes were saved already and others were not, so none of them was saved. | A batch of commands holds commands that were applied already, in another batch, and commands that were not, so nothing of it is applied (PRD FR-API-03). A batch applies whole or not at all, so only a client that grouped its commands anew sends one. `details.applied` lists the `command_id`s of the batch that were applied, in the order of the batch. Send the commands that were not applied in a batch of their own; a batch of commands that were all applied is answered as already applied. |
| `weak_password` | 422 | The password is too weak. | The password breaks the password policy (PRD FR-AUTH-01 AC2). `details.reason` says how: `too_short`, with fewer than 12 characters, counted as Unicode code points once the password is in NFKC, or `common`, one of the 10,000 most common passwords, compared without regard to case. `details.errors` names the field, with its `location` and a `message`, as for `validation_failed`. |
| `image_invalid` | 422 | The file is not an image that can be uploaded. | The uploaded file is not an image that an upload takes (PRD FR-ASSET-02): a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, or SVG image, which the server tells from the file's content, never from its name or the request's `Content-Type`. Nothing is stored. `details.reason` says why: `type`, for a file that is none of them, as text whose name ends in `.png` (FR-ASSET-02 AC1), or an SVG file whose root is not an `svg` element of SVG's namespace; `malformed`, for one that starts as an image does but whose header does not decode, or an SVG file that is not well-formed XML, as one of more than one document type, or one that names no encoding other than UTF-8 but whose bytes are not UTF-8; `unsupported`, for an SVG file that is well-formed, but that is in UTF-16, or declares an encoding other than UTF-8, whatever its bytes, or a version of XML other than 1.0, nests its elements more than 256 deep, has an element of more than 1,024 attributes, or elements that enclose one another and declare more than 1,024 namespaces in all, or whose document type declares an entity that is not text of at most 1,024 bytes, more than 64 entities, or entities whose references expand to more than 4 MiB in all; or `dimensions`, for an image of more than 25,000,000 pixels, or of more than 16,384 on a side. `details.errors` names the body, with its `location` and a `message` that says what is wrong, as for `validation_failed`. An SVG file that holds a script or refers to something outside itself is not refused: the server stores it without them. |
| `slug_invalid` | 422 | The slug must be lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens, and not a reserved word. | A slug is not one that the route or the command takes (PRD FR-TEN-01 AC3, FR-PROJ-02 AC4). A slug is groups of lowercase ASCII letters and digits joined by single hyphens, as `harbour-team`, of at most 64 characters, and not a reserved word: a name that Windows reserves for a device, such as `con` or `com1`, which no slug may be, and, for a workspace's, a word that the product keeps for itself, such as `admin` or `api`. `details.reason` says which rule it breaks: `format` or `reserved`. `details.errors` names the field, with its `location` and a `message`, as for `validation_failed`. |
| `key_invalid` | 422 | A key must be at most 64 ASCII letters, digits, and underscores, not start with a digit, and not be a reserved word. | The key of a variable, a component type, an attribute definition, or a component is not an identifier of the expression language (PRD FR-VAR-01 AC1, FR-COMP-01 AC3, FR-COMP-02 AC1, §5.8.1): an ASCII letter or an underscore, then ASCII letters, digits, and underscores, as `met_elara`, of at most 64 characters, compared case by case, and not one of the language's reserved words, `true`, `false`, `and`, `or`, `not`, `global`, `board`, `null`, `if`, `else`, and `elseif`. `details.reason` says which rule it breaks: `format` or `reserved`. `details.errors` names the field, with its `location` and a `message`, as for `validation_failed`. |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | Too many requests. Try again later. | The client made too many requests (PRD FR-API-04 AC3, NFR-SEC-06), or signing in with an email address failed too often in a row (FR-AUTH-05). The `Retry-After` header says how many seconds to wait. `details.reason` says which: `rate`, when the requests of a kind, its `details.bucket`, used up their limit for the client's IP address, its account, the API token that they are made with, or the email address that they name, until the `RateLimit-Reset` header's seconds have passed; or `locked`, when 10 sign-ins in a row with the email address failed, whether or not it belongs to an account, which locks it for a minute, and each further failure, once a lock ends, for twice as long as the lock before, up to 15 minutes. While the address is locked, `POST /api/v1/auth/login` refuses every sign-in with it, even with the right password. Once the lock ends, the next sign-in is checked: one that succeeds forgets the failures, and one that fails locks the address again. The failures are forgotten a day after the last one. `details.bucket` is `auth` for signing in and the other requests about credentials, among them making, listing, and revoking an API token, which the description of each operation that counts in it lists, and in which no request made with an API token counts, so that a token's requests cannot keep its owner from revoking it; `read` for every other request that reads; and `write` for every other that changes something. Every operation's description states its limits. |
| `internal_error` | 500 | An internal error occurred. | The server failed. Its log has the cause, under the envelope's `request_id`. |
| `not_ready` | 503 | The server is not ready. | The server is starting, its database has pending migrations, or it is stopping. `/readyz` answers with it then too, and also while the server cannot reach its database, which the API's routes report as `internal_error` instead. `details.reason` says which: `starting`, `migrations_pending`, `stopping`, or, from `/readyz` only, `database_unreachable`. A `Retry-After` header suggests when to try again. |
